quest.title: Congenial Gathering
quest.description: You hear that Mondstadt and Liyue are hosting a joint event and decide to take a look...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, looks like you're having fun! What's the occasion this time?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #Ohoho, do I spy {NICKNAME} and a Paimon? We were just talking about you! This is more serendipitous than finding Mora after faceplanting on the road!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It's been too long! I'll bet you have some thrilling new tales from your journey to fill me in on? I can see it in your eyes.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Excellent. I knew I could count on you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What were you talking about before we got here? Something fun? Or... something delicious?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Heh, we were talking about one certain Traveler, and how two's company but three's a crowd as the inseparable duo tour around Teyvat, making four friends here and five more there, often at sixes and sevens as they brave the lakes and seas collecting pieces of eight and countless other treasures. They clearly must have nine lives *wink wink* let's hope they have less than ten deaths...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the... it just gets worse and worse!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Shortly, you may attend a grand banquet at Stone Gate! All will be dressed to the nines for majestic food and fine wines, and after eight long drinks and seven shorts, they'll each write six lines five times. You've been to all four corners of the world, so in three short seconds, can you guess from these two stanzas of one speech each what this event is about?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, it's not, though that does sound fun... Maybe we missed an opportunity.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: In fact, it's a poetry gala, jointly hosted by representatives from both Mondstadt and Liyue!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Do you still remember the promise I made to the distinguished Director Hu here during the Lantern Rite?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, something about writing poetry together?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's right! At the dinner table that night, I just knew this young bard was a rare talent with exceptional taste. You know, it's rare to encounter such a kindred spirit.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And now, I have finally seized the chance to collaborate! It took me much trekking across the land to petition Yujing Terrace and contact the Knights of Favonius, but eventually...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: In the spirit of friendship and poetry-sharing, I managed to successfully organize the "Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bit of a weird name...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Liyue's poetry is known far and wide, and Mondstadt is the "City of Wine and Song"! With two nations teaming up, it'll be double the fun, and a great chance for people from both places to get to know one another!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hu Tao and I will be the co-hosts for this poetry gala. Of course, I haven't studied the various forms and formalities of Liyue poetry for very long, so please forgive my dreadful performance just now.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Not at all, Venti, you followed my lead most excellently!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, you flatter me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, this sounds like fun. Let's get involved!

choices.text: Forsooth, I am wont to dabble in verse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon's sure you'll be amazing! Remember that time in Liyue when Paimon gave you the first half of a couplet, "Windrise's winds never churn"? You came up with the second half right away!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "But the Sea of Clouds' clouds always return."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh, looks like someone's got a knack for this! Perhaps we'll have to raise the difficulty a little.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. So basically, you guys are here to discuss the activities for the poetry gala, right?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh, looks like little Paimon's brain has gained a wrinkle or two! You guessed it so effortlessly! ...But you still guessed it wrong.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, Paimon guessed wrong?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: We came here hoping to invite a special guest...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...I already told you. I'm not going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xiao! You're here too!

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Never having penned a verse myself, how could I hope to judge the poetry of others? Besides, afflicted with karma as I am, the raucous atmosphere you are cultivating is precisely the kind which I must avoid, as you well know.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hey now, there's a first time for everything, right? We all start from "itsy-bitsy spider," but give it a shot and you'll be wandering lonely as a cloud in no time!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And you don't even have to join us in person if you really don't want to. You can just watch the party from a nearby mountaintop and cheer us on.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But at least head down and take a look first? It's right by the inn, and there's plenty of fun activities to get involved with. It can't hurt to take a quick walk and check things out.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Besides, with the renowned {NICKNAME} here, what is there to fear?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Join us. It'll be fun.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I'll consider it.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It's nearly time. Why don't you all head to the venue and take a look around? Quite a few of your friends should have arrived by now.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Yes, that's right! Venti and I still need to discuss the poem for the opening ceremony, so we'll catch up with you later. Plus, our adeptus friend might need a bit more convincing. We'll see if we can coax him down...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gotcha, we'll be on our way then!

choices.text: Sure, I'm looking forward to everyone's poems!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Correct! It's a poetry gala, and Mondstadt and Liyue are hosting it together!

choices.text: Never a dull moment on this Teyvat trip.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...How about that for an opening?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, I like it, but if we could give it a bit more "oomph" it would be even better!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I think we should lead with a bang, dip into a slippedy-slide, then whoosh into a woop-woop! Boom.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Got it?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Got it! Completely understood.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hmm? Well, look who's here! This poetry fest seems to have attracted talent of the highest caliber.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Xingqiu and Chongyun are here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I was actually heading into the mountains to train, but he accosted me on the way and dragged me here.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, how your words wound me! Is it not the responsibility of an exorcist of Liyue to ensure that this celebration of friendship between our two nations stays free of evil spirits?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Besides, this is an excellent opportunity to meet heroes who have come from far and wide. Surely, you must be curious as to how that heroine of Mondstadt was able to lift such heavy objects like they were but a feather?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you talking about Noelle? Yeah, she's super strong!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, since you are so well acquainted, could we trouble you to introduce us later?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Okay, fine... but don't forget to help me with my investigation like you promised. That's the only reason I agreed to come at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Ahem, naturally, I could never forget such a thing. My word is my bond. Relax, dear Paimon, all will be revealed in time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mika! Noelle!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: #Oh! It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Are you here for the Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... you said that with a straight face... Is Paimon the only one who thinks it sounds weird?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you here as Mondstadt's representatives?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: R—Representatives?...? No, nothing fancy like that.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: We were sent here by the Knights of Favonius to help maintain order and set up the venue.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: But... I didn't really do anything useful so far. Noelle brought all these tables and chairs here from Mondstadt by herself... She's a true knight.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Now that's just not true! Your efforts were indispensable — you selected the venue, drew up the layout, and so on. Also, you're the true knight here. I'm still in training! If anything, I should be addressing you as "Sir"...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: What!? No, no, no, no, please don't! Just keep calling me Mika!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does it feel like these two could keep this up all day...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Anyway, Master Jean did say that as long as we keep on top of our work, we should take a look around while we're here and get involved in the poetry gala as much as we can.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: But I haven't written much poetry before, so I'm not sure if I'll fit in...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: I actually have the same concern...

choices.text: The important thing is just to participate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah! Plus you won't be alone — we're joining too! {NICKNAME}'s a really good writer, y'know!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Really? In that case... we'll try our best too!

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Perhaps... the challenge of writing poetry is a rite of passage that all who wish to qualify as a knight must eventually face?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wouldn't go THAT far...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But anyway, no backing out now! See you soon!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Sure! Maybe you can teach me a thing or two!

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Ah, Mika beat me to it! I was gonna ask for help, too...

choices.text: There's a first time for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Diona!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon? I didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you here to mix drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: That's right. I was specially asked to attend this event on behalf of The Cat's Tail, and I'm also here as a mixologist representing the Mondstadt wine industry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're representing Mondstadt's wine industry? You must be hating every minute of it...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Of course I hate it! But it's also a purrfect chance to destroy the reputation of Mondstadt's wine business once and for all. Opportunities like this don't come around every day, y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How do you figure that...?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hehehe, all I need to do is add some gross ingredients to the drinks, and I can create the most disgusting concoctions imaginable! Nobody will ever buy wine from Mondstadt again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Paimon thinks you'll end up getting the opposite result.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmph! Just you wait, I ain't about to mess this up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you gonna write some poetry with us too?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Poetry? Hmm, I've heard plenty of bards sing in the tavern before, but I've never tried writing any myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You should join in. It'll be fun!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...Fine. If I have time.

talks.objective: Take part in the opening event

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A sudden gust of wind forces everyone to briefly shut their eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Poems and melodies wandering the wind, wafting to pastures beyond their home.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Two greedy fishies struggling to swim, they ate so much that they're starting to groan.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Anemo Crystalfly draped in gold robes, a bright little light from that glaze lantern glows.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Finches pinch the rice and scoot, while the boars of the forest anxiously root!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Welcome, one and all, to this festival of poetry, jointly organized by Liyue and Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Or, in full: the "Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala"!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We are your hosts: Liyue's versemonger of the darkest alleys, Hu Tao...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...And Mondstadt's liquor-loving lyricist, Venti the bard!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The purpose of this event is to promote friendly, poetic exchanges between our two nations! So please, have fun, talk to other people, and make some new friends.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If you're here, you're our guest, so please enjoy this poetry fest!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I'd also like to reassure everyone that this event welcomes people of all skill levels, from first-time rhymers to seasoned songwriters.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If you ask me, the most important thing you can bring to writing poetry is authenticity. That means reaching deep down to all the thoughts and feelings you usually hide away or struggle to express, and putting them into words... Just write from the heart, in whatever form you like.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: To help everyone really cut loose and enjoy themselves to the fullest, Venti and I have carefully prepared three themes, to be revealed over the course of three days!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Let's get right to it! The first theme is... "Riddle Me This"!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: (Solving riddles, huh? Interesting. It's actually a pretty good choice for a warm-up activity.)

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (Whew... I'm glad they're not making us write sonnets or something right at the start.)

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Does everyone see the lanterns hanging around the venue? These have been specially prepared for the riddle game.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Simply write down your riddle and hang it on a lantern. Then, Venti and I will select a few to pose to the crowd, and you will try to solve them!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We'll now give you some time to write down and hang up your riddles. Feel free to walk around and talk with the other contestants to get the creative juices flowing. And remember, whoever guesses the most riddles correctly will get a prize!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And with that, the "Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala" has officially begun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, let's see what's on this lantern...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... "A tender sigh for home, how far the flowers roam. A visitor asks me 'why': For a dream beyond the sky."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, someone from Liyue definitely wrote this one.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: I just read that one too! Liyue's poems seem pretty difficult to grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Dreams... sky... is it talking about some kind of bird?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm, so it means something like... This thing's really far from home, it's in a vast area, and it's flying really high... Is that it?

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Oh, you're amazing, Paimon! It looks like I still have a lot of learning to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw... It's nothing, really. Once you've spent enough time in Liyue, you just sort of pick up on these things.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Oh, I know exactly what you mean. Back when I was out with the Grand Master on the expedition, I started picking up some local customs without even realizing it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But back to the riddle — we still haven't actually solved it. What could it be talking about?

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Something that flies high and far... Oh, that makes me think of dandelions.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Oh! That makes sense. And Mondstadters believe that dandelions can carry your feelings on the wind.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: But maybe we're missing something? It can't be that easy. After all, it's a riddle from Liyue... What would their equivalent of the dandelion be? If there even is one...

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think "dandelion" is the right answer.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Great! Then we'll have one answer ready to go when the game begins.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The important thing is that it's authentic.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Right, just like Venti said! As long as the interpretation makes sense, and reflects our perception of the poem, then perhaps there are no wrong answers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, no matter what the real answer is, the guessing's all part of the fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go look at the next one!

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Yes! I want to see if there's any Mondstadt-style riddles.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one says... ugh... this handwriting is just awful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ..."I have four corners like a square pancake, but I'm stuffed and seasoned and carefully baked. I pass through the lips one piece at a time, the more you consume, the broader your mind."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon's drooling from that one! Is there really a food that can make you smarter? Paimon's gotta try that!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Haha, oh Paimon, you have to look past the surface-level meaning with riddles, or you'll fail to plumb their depths.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So, have you got any ideas, Xingqiu?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Heh, well...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Xingqiu just hung that riddle up a moment ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So this is Xingqiu's riddle! Y'know, Paimon was expecting you to write something a little more... elegant.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: This festival is about building friendship and mutual understanding. With so many friends from Mondstadt present, I thought I'd try writing something more accessible and less flowery, so that more people could enjoy it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, not bad! So, buddy, does that mean you can tell your old pal Paimon the answer on the sly...?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Not a chance. You'll have to wait for the answer to be revealed just like everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Meanie.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: If that's how you feel, why don't you try and stump me with a riddle of your own?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: M—Maybe Paimon will! We'll see who stumps who!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}, you'll help Paimon come up with a riddle, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Gladly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, at least you're nice to Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Haha, then I look forward to seeing the fruits of your literary labors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Prepare to get stumped!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Even though Paimon said she'd write a riddle, Paimon really doesn't have any clue how.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's start by reading a few more of other people's for inspiration...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "On four long legs my slim body sits, I eat not a bite and drink not a sip. With a passionless face I greet countless guests, whom I carry all day without needing to rest."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Is this talking about some kind of animal?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: It's a chair!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Diona, how'd you guess it so quickly? Wait, were you the one who wrote it?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: No, of course I didn't write it! The answer just popped into my head.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I'm always telling the cats in the tavern that the chairs get tired from working all the time, so they shouldn't use them to sharpen their claws.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... So a riddle needs to have a bait-and-switch...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Are you tryna write one?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! And thanks to you, Paimon's just thought of one!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Maybe I should try and come up with one, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, alright, Paimon's riddle is now hanging up! ....Diona, do you wanna know the answer?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Nah, no need. I don't really care about winning a prize.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay then... Well, looks like it's time to carry on with the event. We should regroup with the others.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Sure. Have fun!

choices.text: The answer must be some other kind of object.

talks.objective: Wait until the start of the riddle-solving event

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Heyo, looks like everyone's about done mingling and riddling! Gather round, and look this way!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Venti and I have selected several riddles from everyone's contributions, and we added a few of our own to the mix for good measure. Shortly, we'll randomly select a few to read aloud.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If your riddle gets selected, remember that you have to announce the correct answer at the end. Anyone who guesses correctly gets one point, and if nobody guesses correctly, the writer of the riddle gets a point. Sounds fair to me!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Of course, when the riddler reveals the right response, it only counts if everyone agrees that it's not too far-fetched!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's right! Now, if there are no more questions, it's time to reveal the first riddle!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (...Hopefully they'll draw at least some that I can get. Oh no, does only the first person to solve it get the points? ...Ugh, that means I have to be first to raise my hand...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Please choose Paimon's riddle, please choose Paimon's riddle...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Riddle number one! Let me see here... Uh, this riddle is, uh... unique. Especially the handwriting...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ..."I have... poor... cor—four! Four corners like a square... pancake? But I'm st—stuffed and seasoned? And carefully bu—baked. (Baked? Baked.) I pass through the... chips? Lips! ...uh, one piece at a time, the more you... uh, c—consume, consume, consume! The broader your f—mind."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They drew Xingqiu's!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Better answer as quickly as you can. You don't want someone else beating you to it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You! Drat! Um... it's, uh... PIZZA! The answer is pizza!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ehhh... Even without the author coming forward, I can confidently declare this answer wrong! How does eating pizza broaden your mind!?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And while I'm no expert in exotic dishes... If I'm not mistaken, pizza is round, is it not? Like Mora Meat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... eating pizza makes you happy, and being happy makes it easier to face problems that need solving, sooo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, Paimon admits she may have jumped the gun on this one...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: (Maybe it's some other kind of food? No no no no, riddles are never that simple, and it needs to be something that makes people more intelligent...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Paimon had known it was gonna be this tough, she'd have read more books in her time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What is it? Have you got it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Books"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh?

choices.text: They're square, and they've got lots of big words baked into them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Gotcha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Books! The answer is books!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Haha, that was quicker than I expected! I was quite proud of that one.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh? It appears the riddle-writer has announced the answer! Okay, one point to Paimon!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (Huh? So the answer was "books"? Argh, how did I not get that? C'mon Mika, concentrate...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, we're awesome at this!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Ahem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh... Uh, what Paimon meant to say was that you're awesome at this! Thanks for the point, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: On to riddle number two!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (I gotta get in there first this time...)

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: "High above the wispy clouds, amidst the gloomy snow-filled shroud, standing alone on an icy stage, beneath it every lowly sage." Looks like a poem from Liyue!

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Oh! It's—

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: I got it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Looks like those two have some ideas. Hmm, could it be some kind of plant that lives in cold, high places?

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Mika, please go ahead. As a full Knight of Favonius, you represent all of us from Mondstadt here.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: No, no, how could I? It was you who thought of it first. You should be the one to guess.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: My answer isn't necessarily correct. Besides, it's first-come, first-served, and you beat me to it...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: N—No I didn't... You were just before me...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, how gracious and considerate our fellow competitors are towards each other. A wonderful sight to see.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: How about both of you say your answer at the same time? If you're both right, you'll each get a point.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: (Whoops, I didn't realize we'd made such a scene...)

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (Oh, crud... Guess we dragged that out a bit...)

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Um... So Noelle, what do you say...

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Yes, let's. Our answer is:

response.speaker: Mika & Noelle
response.text: "Cecilia."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That certainly sounds like a good candidate for the correct answer! A flower that blooms on the highest peaks and known for its exquisite beauty, the Cecilia is held by many Mondstadters to be the true "Windblume."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Uh... Although since the writer hasn't yet come forward to announce the answer, this probably wasn't the answer they were looking for. Sorry! Any other answers?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (I can't believe I was wrong... Maybe it's a plant from Liyue?)

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: ...Is the answer "Qingxin"? The poem does evoke a strong sense of quiet, proud solitude in a high place.

response.speaker: Riddle Writer
response.text: Correct! I wrote this one. Qingxin is the right answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nooo! Xingqiu got it before Paimon could!

response.speaker: Riddle Writer
response.text: ...However, after listening to the host's description, I do remember reading about Cecilia flowers in a book once. They definitely fit the description of a pure flower standing proudly and alone on high.

response.speaker: Riddle Writer
response.text: So, I'd like to approve the answer from our two friends from Mondstadt as well.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Really? Thank you so much...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha! Well, since even the riddler themself agrees, all three contestants earn a point each!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Darn it! Xingqiu's caught up to Paimon already!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... You're probably right.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Moving now to our third riddle... Huh? Why is the handwriting so... floaty...?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "What's got no wings but flies in the air, never gets tired of floating up there, so full of Mora it comes out the nose, but in the sea glug glug glug down it goes!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's Paimon's! They picked Paimon's riddle! Yay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it? Why isn't anyone guessing? Is Paimon's riddle too hard?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: That's not quite it. More like... it's so ludicrously simple that we just cannot believe it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? No way... Well, go on then, tell us the answer if you're so sure.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: The answer is... "Paimon."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: It's "Paimon."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's "Paimon."

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: I was actually gonna say "Paimon," too...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Me too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! You're all completely wrong! How the heck did you all think the answer was Paimon!?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Paimon, do you have wings behind your back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, no.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: You're always floating, but you never seem to get tired of it.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: #And Paimon has a very healthy appetite, which must cost {NICKNAME} a lot of Mora in meal expenses.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: #I've heard from the senior knights that {NICKNAME} rescued Paimon by fishing her out of the sea. So, that means Paimon can't swim, so if she fell in the sea, then, uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Glug glug glug...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, wait... Now Paimon's doubting herself, what was the answer again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Think about it for a moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, you're all wrong! The answer to Paimon's riddle is obviously the "Jade Chamber"! You know, the Jade Chamber that's always flying up there in the sky!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Is that so? Hmm, I still maintain that the riddle actually describes "Paimon" more accurately.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: In fact, if we just added two more lines to the poem, it would be the perfect riddle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you want to add?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: ..."The Traveler's companion and talkative guide, a praiseworthy presence always by their side."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, do you mean it? Can we really add that part?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think so too? Hee-hee...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Then Paimon would like to announce that the correct answer to the riddle is... the widely adored "Paimon"!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Great! And with that, the widely adored Paimon has gifted a point each to everyone who answered just now!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: More riddles and giggles fill the air as the time flies by...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, guessing riddles is a lot of fun. And even though Paimon didn't manage to beat Xingqiu, Paimon still feels like she got a little smarter!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh — didn't Chongyun mention he was investigating something before? Let's go ask him about it.

choices.text: Paimon's the best travel companion ever!
Every big word that passes through your lips as you read it out makes you smarter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey you two!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh? Hi Paimon. You know, for a moment there, I was worried I might lose to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Ooh, are you collecting your prize right now?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I am indeed! Though if you really want it, I'd be more than happy to give it to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously!? Wow, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Ummm...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: A most generous donation by yours truly as Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Namely, a buy one get one free coupon for our high-end customized service package! It's a pleasant surprise to learn you're so interested in it, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hahahaha! Nope! Nuh-uh, no thank you! Hard pass — you can keep it!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Are you sure? In that case, I'll gladly take it!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Here you are! Now remember, this package comes with our "anytime, anywhere" on-demand collection service! Just give us a call and we'll be right there! ...With any luck, we'll still show up even if you're... unable to call.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: So, to what do we owe the honor, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! What do you mean, "we"? Chongyun's the one Paimon's looking for, not you. Wasn't he saying something about needing help?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, that...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: How about I put it in riddle form?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't the competition over?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: "'Twas like a demon not demonic, or devil devoid of the diabolic. Afar it floated free above the ground, but when approached, though sought, nought could be found."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sounds to me like you encountered a ghastly little ghostie in the wild?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should just explain it...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Basically, while I was training this morning, I suddenly caught sight of a nonhuman entity.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It was floating in the air without any kind of external aid, and its body was almost transparent. At first, I thought I'd finally encountered a demon that wasn't repelled by my pure-yang spirit, and immediately prepared to exorcise it.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: But none of my methods had any effect on it. And when I went to try and get a closer look at it and try to ascertain what I was dealing with, it disappeared into thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're sure it's not a ghost or spirit of some kind?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Quite sure. I could sense that it had a physical body. And if it were a spirit, I'm sure it would have been scared away long before I saw it.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It's all my fault. I got overexcited, and in my haste I didn't ascertain its true nature before taking action. Thinking back on it... If it wasn't an evil spirit, maybe I offended some kind of adeptus, or illuminated beast...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You shouldn't blame yourself. It was something you'd never seen before — anyone else would've reacted the same way.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Besides, we're making up for it now by doing our best to find out the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Any thoughts, Venti? Have you managed to untangle Chongyun's twisted tale?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Why don't you take a guess first, Hu Tao?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oho, that means you have!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, I can't be absolutely certain, but I'm reasonably sure it's not what Liyue would call an "evil spirit" or "demon." So whatever it is, it's not dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... How about this? We can incorporate a "search" element into tomorrow's poetry activity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, does that mean we get to play outside while we write poetry?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, close! ...But no.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Good ideas could just pop into your head out of thin air. But if you ask me, everyone should relax tonight, and get a good rest before tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You say that, but your gaze keeps drifting over towards the wine stand!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: What do you think the key to a good poem is, Mika? Do you have any idea?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Huh? I, uh... I'm not too sure either.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: If I'd known we'd be doing this sooner... I would've asked Miss Lisa to recommend some books on the topic.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Are you sure that wasn't really an evil spirit?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Open your mind to all possibilities, and I'm sure you will find the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I suppose that's true... Hey, wait a second, you're not planning on telling everyone here, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Now, should I try adding Loach Pearls or Horsetails next...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Ooh, wait! Since we're in Liyue, I should add some Jueyun Chilis!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, that was a good little opening ceremony, wasn't it? Even if I do say so myself.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We couldn't cajole Adeptus Xiao in the end. He said he'd take a peek from the peaks, but that was all he'd agree to. It's a real shame — I had the perfect poem for his entrance and everything.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Seeing my friends having such a lively discussion, I couldn't help but join in on the fun.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Of course, I promised Hu Tao I'd behave and do my job as a good host... but I really am parched from speaking so much. It would be negligent not to wet my whistle.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And you know what the best part is? Wine is to the poet's tongue as ink to his pen. So, two birds with one stone!

dialogues.speaker: Poetry Riddle on a Lantern
dialogues.text: Hmm... "A tender sigh for home, how far the flowers roam. A visitor asks me 'why': For a dream beyond the sky."

dialogues.speaker: Poetry Riddle on a Lantern
dialogues.text: ..."I have four corners like a square pancake, but I'm stuffed and seasoned and carefully baked. I pass through the lips one piece at a time, the more you consume, the broader your mind."

dialogues.speaker: Poetry Riddle on a Lantern
dialogues.text: "On four long legs my slim body sits, I eat not a bite and drink not a sip. With a passionless face I greet countless guests, whom I carry all day without needing to rest."

dialogues.speaker: Poetry Riddle on a Lantern
dialogues.text: "What's got no wings but flies in the air, never gets tired of floating up there, so full of Mora it comes out the nose, but in the sea glug glug glug down it goes!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so lively! Didn't think there'd be so many people here already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And a lot of them are familiar faces. Let's go say hi!
